methods.label: Factor the difference of squares
methods.explanation:
Let \(b\) be the length of the second arm. Since the hypotenuse is the longest side, \(c>a\). The two lengths are consecutive integers, so \(c-a=1\).

By the Pythagorean theorem, the square we want is \(b^2=c^2-a^2\). Factoring exposes the known difference \(c-a\):
\[
b^2=(c-a)(c+a)=1\cdot(c+a)=c+a.
\]
Thus the square of the second arm is \(\boxed{c+a}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
methods.levelReason: Uses the Pythagorean theorem and elementary difference-of-squares factoring.
